item.title: 2025 Was a Great Year for the F-35 Program, Lockheed Martin Says
item.description: Lockheed Martin reported producing a record-breaking number of F-35s in 2025, and expanding its orders abroad—even as some nations have scaled back or withdrawn from the program. item.title: How China’s Nuclear Obfuscation Could End the World
item.description: China has intentionally chosen to hide its nuclear doctrine as a core part of its strategy—exponentially increasing the risk of a nuclear catastrophe. The post How China’s Nuclear Obfuscation Could End the World appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The New Pinaka LRGR-120 Missile: A Quiet Revolution in Indian Doctrine
item.description: India’s new Pinaka LRGR-120 is roughly comparable to an American HIMARS rocket—but was built entirely within India, with capabilities that could be improved over time. The post The New Pinaka LRGR-120 Missile: A Quiet Revolution in Indian Doctrine appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Shoot, Scoot, Survive: Israel’s New Self-Propelled Howitzer
item.description: The SIGMA 155 self-propelled howitzer includes multiple new innovations—including an autoloader, speeding up reload times and allowing it to more easily reposition after each shot. The post Shoot, Scoot, Survive: Israel’s New Self-Propelled Howitzer appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: YJ-20: Meet the Chinese Missile Built to Break the US Navy
item.description: The YJ-20 is particularly concerning for American defense planners because large US ships still have no reliable countermeasures against hypersonic weapons. The post YJ-20: Meet the Chinese Missile Built to Break the US Navy appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Italy Is Breaking Ground on Europe’s First F-35 Training Center
item.description: The new training center for F-35 fighter pilots—the first outside of the United States—is expected to be operational by 2028. The post Italy Is Breaking Ground on Europe’s First F-35 Training Center appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: New Pentagon Inspector General Report Highlights F-35 Shortfalls
item.description: The inspector general’s report criticized Lockheed Martin’s systemic inability to meet contract requirements, as well as the F-35’s dismal readiness rate. The post New Pentagon Inspector General Report Highlights F-35 Shortfalls appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: France, UK Pledge Troops to Defend Ukraine—but Only After War Ends
item.description: Even the most optimistic estimates suggest that Britain and France could only scrape together 15,000 troops for deployment in Ukraine—far too few to deter a future Russian invasion.
